function to get interpolated event locked data

Source: R/event_lock_timeseries.R
event_lock_ts.Rd

function to get interpolated event locked data

Usage

event_lock_ts(
  fmri_obj,
  event = NULL,
  time_before = -3,
  time_after = 3,
  collide_before = NULL,
  collide_after = NULL,
  pad_before = -1,
  pad_after = 1,
  time_audit = FALSE,
  overlap_policy = NULL,
  valid_col = NULL,
  neighbor_events = NULL
)

Arguments

fmri_obj

An fmri_ts object containing time series data that are optionally keyed on one or more grouping variables (e.g., ROI). The fmri_obj must also contain trial-level data (in the $event_data field) for event-locking to proceed.

event

Name of column in fmri_obj$event_data that identifies onset for event of interest

time_before

How many seconds before the event do we want data. Default: -3

time_after

How many seconds after the event do we want data. Default: 3

collide_before

An optional vector of column names in trial_df that set a boundary on the earliest time point used in interpolation. This effectively truncates the time series for interpolation to a smaller window than specified by time_before.

collide_after

An optional vector of column names in trial_df that set a boundary on the latest time point used in interpolation. This effectively truncates the time series for interpolation to a smaller window than specified by time_after.

pad_before

Number of seconds to include in the epoch time window before the event of interest. Interpolation spans the window from time_before to time_after, but padding includes data points at the boundary that can help to have sufficient data to interpolate early and late times within the epoch.

pad_after

Number of seconds to include in the epoch time window after the event of interest.

time_audit

If TRUE, additional columns will be added to the output showing how alignment is calculated vis-a-vis event timing

overlap_policy

One of "allow", "truncate", or "exclude". NULL uses truncation when collision columns are supplied and allows overlap otherwise. Explicit allow retains full windows. Exclude removes whole epochs whose closed requested windows overlap another target epoch, including ties.

valid_col

Optional logical source-data column. FALSE or NA censors that row for all value columns without deleting its acquisition time.

neighbor_events

Event columns used for nearest-event annotations; defaults to the target event column. Does not itself censor observations.

Details

Nonfinite target onsets and unsupported windows retain placeholder rows with missing time and values and an epoch_status column. Nonfinite collision candidates are ignored. Nearest-event boundaries remain strict and do not guarantee disjoint trial windows.
